fields.statement: QA cycle 3, hands-on with a scratch build of the branch head (rhiza session run in a scratch repo, fake claude and rex on PATH, isolated HOME). The agent wrote Claude Code's synthetic usage-limit line with a reset 6s ahead. The run waited 6s, and session show read working, 'paused at its usage limit until <reset>', during the wait. It then relaunched claude with --resume and the same session ID, told 'The usage limit has reset. Continue where you left off.' as the last arg. No second --session-id launch, exit 0. An agent left open at its limit (sleeping) was killed by the 30s watcher and resumed (elapsed 30s). An agent limited every time got 1 start and 24 resumes, then the session failed: 'still stopped at its usage limit after 24 pauses'. Via rhiza session hook: a Stop hook with the synthetic 'hit your limit' line last recorded working 'paused at its usage limit'. A normal Stop, and a later model turn quoting 'usage limit reached|1700000000' and 'hit your limit', recorded idle.

QA cycle 3, hands-on with a scratch build: rhiza run start --workflow one (a single agent step) in a scratch repo, with a fake rex that runs the tab command and a fake claude. On first launch the fake wrote the synthetic usage-limit line (reset 4s ahead) and deleted the transcript 2s later. After the wait, the run relaunched claude with --session-id, not --resume: a fresh session for the step. The step passed. The run journal (.git/rhiza/runs/<run>.jsonl) gained a fresh-session entry for step build and that session, and the session record's fresh list got a timestamp. session run printed the warning that the transcript was gone and a fresh session was started instead of resuming.
